answer: Each kiln load is counted brick by brick, and the brickmaker's tally holds the number fired in every load of the season. A orchard cart of bricks bought from another yard fails the tally: at the relic of the kiln the bricks must bear the yard's own stamp, and bought bricks carry another maker's mark. Faking a season means building a kiln, burning 20,000 bricks and paying 11,900 in clay and coal, while the cedar stamp on every brick is read at the building site, so a load whose tally was never entered is turned away.
